plan.title: Liver RNA-seq: 3-group LRT + per-treatment contrasts
plan.analytical_narrative:
The data are gene-level Salmon counts for 12 human liver samples (12,000 genes x 13 columns in counts.csv — one gene-id column plus 12 sample columns) with metadata.csv giving one condition per sample: control, treated_a, treated_b, four replicates each, unpaired, single batch. The research question has two parts, and they map onto two different tests. 'Which genes differ across the three groups at all' is an omnibus question that spans two model coefficients, so it is answered by the DESeq2 likelihood ratio test of the full design ~ condition against the reduced design ~ 1. 'Which genes does each treatment change relative to control' is answered by two named Wald contrasts, condition treated_a vs control and condition treated_b vs control, with control set as the explicit reference level (never left to alphabetical ordering). Because the design has three levels, log2 fold changes are shrunk with ashr, which accepts a contrast, rather than apeglm, which accepts only a coefficient. BH adjustment is applied within each contrast at alpha 0.05 with DESeq2 independent filtering on, and the p-value histogram is inspected before the adjustment is trusted.

One caveat is structural and must be carried into the report: the profile records the counts as 'gene-level counts from salmon as delivered; the record does not say whether the length correction occurred'. No per-sample quant.sf files and no average-transcript-length table are present in the inputs, so the length offset cannot be reconstructed. tximport is NOT run on a gene-level table. The model is fitted on the counts as delivered with no length offset, and the report states that a shift in isoform usage can appear as differential expression.

Step T1S1 does sample-structure QC before any test (blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes) — with n=4 per group an outlier sample materially changes the result, so it must be seen first. T1S2 fits the model and produces the omnibus and both contrast tables. T2S1 adds pathway context: the user did not ask for pathways, so enrichment is kept strictly secondary and interpretive, run once per contrast on the full ranked list of tested genes (ranked by the DESeq2 Wald stat — the disputed ranking choice is settled here in favour of the Wald statistic because it scales the effect by its uncertainty), against MSigDB Hallmark and then human Reactome/WikiPathways, each with its release stated. T1S3 assembles the report with MA and dispersion plots, both shrunken and unshrunken effect sizes, and a full reproducibility record.

Power is the honest limit: four replicates per group is at the low end, so absence of significant genes in a contrast is not evidence of no effect, and the report must say so rather than reaching for unadjusted p-values.

~ condition with explicit reference level control
Benjamini-Hochberg within contrast with independent filtering
fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic
reproducible report with MA plot, dispersion plot, session info

The human WikiPathways GMT is present in the reference store and is keyed on HGNC symbols; the hallmark collection was reported present as MSigDB human hallmark gene sets. If a Reactome collection is not resolvable in this environment, say so plainly and report the hallmark and WikiPathways results — this step is interpretive context and its partial loss must not be presented as a failure of the analysis. Match the gene identifier space of the ranked list to that of each collection (map symbols with the human organism annotation package where required) and report the share of tested genes that failed to map. Restrict to sets with 15 to 500 members among the tested genes, adjust with BH, collapse redundant significant sets and report one representative per group, and list the leading-edge genes with their gene-level statistic for each significant set. Finally, report which pathways are significant in both treatment contrasts and which are specific to one.
steps.context: Enrichment was not part of the stated research question — it is included only as secondary interpretive context for the two treatment-vs-control gene lists. The 12,000 genes in the count matrix, not the whole genome, define the tested universe.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea is run once per contrast (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control) on the full ranked list of tested genes
The ranking metric is the DESeq2 Wald statistic, and this choice is stated in the output
Hallmark results are reported first, with Reactome and WikiPathways in separate tables, each with its collection release named
The gene set size window (15 to 500 among tested genes) and BH adjustment are applied and reported
The share of tested genes that failed identifier mapping is reported per collection
Redundant significant sets are collapsed to representatives, with the full table kept as a supplement
Leading-edge genes with their statistic are listed for each significant set
Pathways shared between the two treatment contrasts versus specific to one are tabulated
If a collection cannot be resolved in the environment, that is stated explicitly rather than silently substituted
constraints: Use the full ranked list of every tested gene; do not pre-cut by adjusted p-value or fold change
Run enrichment once per contrast; do not pool genes from the two contrasts into a single list
Use human gene set collections only — the samples are Homo sapiens
Keep each collection's results in its own table; do not merge collections into a single set list
Do not attempt any network download; resolve collections from the provisioned reference store only
Set and record a random seed — fgsea permutation results are not reproducible without it
caveats: If fewer than about 50 genes are significant in a contrast, do not fall back to an over-representation test on that short list; the preranked method on the full list is the correct and only test here.
Enrichment results depend strongly on the method and the collection. Present each set as a hypothesis for follow-up, not as an established finding.
Gene length and expression level bias enrichment of count data; the tested genes define the universe, which removes only the detection-driven part of that bias.

steps.name: Report and reproducibility record
steps.question: What is the consolidated answer: how many genes differ across control, treated_a and treated_b at all, how many change in each treatment relative to control, how much do the two treatment responses overlap, and under what stated limitations?
steps.description: Assemble the final report from T1S2 and T2S1. Lead with the two direct answers: the number of genes with an LRT adjusted p-value below 0.05 (differ across the three groups at all) and the number at padj < 0.05 in each of treated_a vs control and treated_b vs control. Give the overlap of the two treatment gene lists — shared responders versus treatment-specific — as a Venn or UpSet plot plus a table, and a scatter of the shrunken log2 fold changes of treated_a vs treated_b over the LRT-significant genes, which shows directly whether the two treatments move the liver transcriptome the same way or differently. Include the DESeq2 fit diagnostics before the gene tables: MA plot per contrast (shrunken values) and the dispersion estimate plot. Include a heatmap of VST values for the top LRT-significant genes, samples grouped by condition. Gene tables carry baseMean, unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, ashr-shrunken log2FoldChange, stat, pvalue, padj and the contrast label; rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken fold change, never on the unshrunken value alone. State the method, every package version, the design formula ~ condition, the reference level control, each named contrast, alpha = 0.05 with BH within contrast, the number of genes tested after filtering out of 12,000, and the number of DE genes per contrast. State the enrichment collections with their releases, the Wald-statistic ranking metric, the tested-gene universe and the 15-500 size window, and note that enrichment results are method-dependent hypotheses. Attach sessionInfo, the random seed used for fgsea permutations, and package versions. Explicitly record the two standing limitations: the Salmon length offset could not be applied because no quantification files or transcript length table were supplied, so isoform-usage shifts can masquerade as differential expression; and four replicates per group is low power, so an empty contrast is not evidence of no effect.

constraints: Do not compute any new statistical test in this step
Do not report any gene list selected by unadjusted p-value or by fold change alone

Shared pathway hits between treated_a and treated_b may reflect a shared handling or vehicle effect rather than a shared mechanism; this design cannot separate the two.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
